title: Reading Test 2: The Changing Role of Libraries

passage.label: A
passage.text: Community libraries have changed considerably over the last century. In the past, many libraries were quiet rooms where visitors borrowed printed books and read newspapers. Today, they often provide internet access, digital catalogues, study spaces, children’s activities, and advice sessions for local residents.

passage.label: B
passage.text: One reason for this change is the development of digital information. As more services moved online, libraries became important places for people who did not have reliable internet access at home. Staff members began to help users complete online forms, search for jobs, and use basic computer software.

passage.label: C
passage.text: Libraries also support social connection. In some neighbourhoods, weekly reading groups and craft clubs are among the few regular activities open to people of different ages. This role is especially valuable for older residents, new parents, and people who have recently moved to an area.

passage.label: D
passage.text: However, libraries face financial pressure. Local authorities may reduce opening hours or close smaller branches when budgets are limited. Supporters argue that these decisions save money only in the short term because libraries also reduce pressure on other public services by improving literacy, confidence, and access to information.

passage.label: E
passage.text: The future library is unlikely to be defined only by the number of books on its shelves. Instead, its value may depend on how effectively it combines physical space, digital support, and community activity. For many users, the library remains a public place where help can be found without payment or appointment.
